confidence_notes: I ran four web searches: one for the RBA rate and three for Essaouira food and drink prices. The price results were mostly crowdsourced cost-of-living and travel-guide aggregators (Numbeo-style data, Jobicy, Nomad Watch, TripBase, a Lonely Planet spending diary), and they disagree. Restaurant meals and coffee are reasonably supported: budget meals were about $4-5, cappuccino about $1.5-3, and medina mid-range dinners about 200-350 MAD per person against $14-20 in the aggregators. I set the mid-range anchor for two between those, for a tourist-area three-course meal. Beer was $2-4.6 in the sources; I used a licensed-restaurant price, since alcohol is limited in Essaouira. Cocktail and wine are the least certain. Sources gave cocktails of about $5.4 (average) to $9, and wine of about $7 per glass from one traveller report plus bottle prices of 40-60 MAD, so I set them by their usual relationship to beer and tourist-venue pricing. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates only; I searched no accommodation prices and inspected no listings. They are scaled for July peak-season demand in a popular Atlantic coastal tourist town with many riads and guesthouses.
comparable_city_reasoning: Essaouira's own aggregated price data, cross-checked against other Moroccan tourist cities such as Marrakech and Taghazout. Prices are somewhat lower than Marrakech for food, but beer, cocktails and wine are priced at tourist-venue levels because of limited alcohol licensing.
